hypothesis_drift: UNNAMED FIGURE TYPE (address.py:431): 'ORDER' with no source, no integration time and no statement of whether 1e-9 is a noise, stability or accuracy figure. gravimetric_radius (address.py:724-726) uses it as an instantaneous absolute detection threshold for a STATIC source. Whether any existing instrument meets that use at 1e-9 is exactly the part not READ here. This is a hypothesis the tree leaves unnamed, not an error shown.

ADDED/UNNAMED BACKGROUND HYPOTHESIS (address.py:213-215, 801-804): 'readable' presumes the source's field is separable from Earth's own field (9.8 m/s^2; the floor is 1.02e-10 g, computed C1) and its time variations at 1e-9. A static source is read either by modulation (moving source or instrument) or against a background model at that level. The size of the backgrounds is NOT READ in this run, so no claim is made that the separation fails -- it is recorded as a hypothesis the prose does not name.

MAGNITUDE vs ONE COMPONENT (address.py:724-726): a gravimeter reads one axis. Computed (C4, sympy): for a surface source seen from Earth's surface the vertical fraction is sin(theta/2) = s/(2 R_E), and the vertical component at the antipode is 1.16e-9 (H1) / 4.03e-9 (H2) m/s^2 -- still above 1e-9, so the one-axis reading does NOT shorten the claim for surface geometry. It is recorded because the magnitude reach 1.37e7 m (H1) exceeds Earth's diameter 1.274e7 m: '1.4e7 m' is a field-strength radius, not a realisable terrestrial baseline. Discrepancy of framing, not of number.

NEWTONIAN POINT MASS (canonical hypothesis): not a drift -- exact for a uniform sphere's exterior (shell theorem) and the post-Newtonian parameter at the reach is 1.5e-19 (H1) / 2.9e-19 (H2) (computed C4b).

FLOOR-DEPENDENT PIN (address.py:1467-1468 selftest 'beats the Higgs standoff by more than 1e23', and the '23 ORDERS' heading at address.py:209 / 'twenty-three orders' at :1215): computed C3, the >1e23 pin holds only for a floor below 6.26e-9 (H1) / 2.15e-8 (H2) m/s^2 -- 6.3x the ORDER value for H1. At a 1 microGal (1e-8) floor H1 gives r/d = 7.9e22 (log10 22.90). The prose '23 orders' survives as rounding; the >1e23 selftest pin does not. The load-bearing prose claim 'MORE THAN TWENTY ORDERS' (address.py:217) holds for any floor below 6.26e-3 (H1) / 2.15e-2 (H2) m/s^2, i.e. 6.3e6 x the ORDER value.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. The 'data' here is the tree's own ORDER value with no cited measurement, and the measurement literature could not be read in this run, so what instrument builders have achieved (and whether it is a noise, stability or accuracy figure) is NOT established here either way. Evidence AGAINST missing data mattering to the conclusion (computed, C3): the floor enters only as a square root; the dependent verdict 'strictly dominated by more than twenty orders' survives any floor up to 6.26e-3 m/s^2 (H1), 6.3e6 times the ORDER value, and gravity out-reads the Higgs (r > d) for any floor up to ~6e37 m/s^2. Evidence FOR something the tree does not have: (a) the >1e23 selftest pin and the precise '1.4e7 m / 2.6e7 m' reach figures move with the floor (r/d falls to 7.9e22 for H1 at 1e-8); (b) the static-source separation hypothesis is unnamed and its background magnitudes were not read. Neither reaches the verdict.
grade_evidence: The result is a MEASUREMENT (the achieved floor of a gravimeter), and no measurement source could be read: alphaXiv refused all three tools (quota exceeded, 4 attempts) and arxiv.org / export.arxiv.org / semanticscholar.org were 403 at the egress proxy; the tree itself cites no source and labels the value ORDER. Under M's rule a claim that cannot be checked here is OPEN, not STANDS. What WAS checked (sympy + numeric, 21 PASS): the unit identity is exact; the reach numbers reproduce; the load-bearing conclusion that rests on the floor ('more than twenty orders', S6) is insensitive to the floor below 6.26e-3 m/s^2, so an eventual reading of the floor cannot move that verdict unless the achievable floor were worse than 6.26e-3 m/s^2 (H1) / 2.15e-2 (H2). Discrepancies recorded, nothing repaired: the selftest pin r/d > 1e23 (address.py:1468) is floor-dependent at a factor 6.3 (H1); the static-source background hypothesis and the figure type (noise/stability/accuracy) are unnamed at address.py:213-215, 431.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: reading a measurement paper (e.g. arXiv:1512.05660 or a superconducting-gravimeter noise study) that shows a static-source gravity difference resolved at <= ~1e-9 m/s^2, with its integration time and background treatment, matching the tree's use. To NARROWED: a read source showing 1e-9 is reached only as a noise/stability figure after long integration or only for time-varying signals, with absolute/static resolution coarser (the verdict would still stand by C3 unless the floor exceeded 6.26e-3 m/s^2; the >1e23 pin would narrow above 6.26e-9). To DATA-DEPENDENT: a read achievable floor above 6.26e-9 m/s^2 moves the >1e23 pin (not the >20-orders verdict). To WRONG: nothing plausible -- it would require no gravimeter resolving 6.26e-3 m/s^2. (The tree's positive control at address.py:1469-1471 checks the Newton formula against g = 9.8, not any instrument's resolution, so it is not evidence here either way.)
